pass1.text: The title says attention is all you need. Before reading the method: which standard part of 2017 translation models do you think they removed, and what does a model lose about a sentence once that part is gone?
The abstract claims better quality AND less training time. Predict where the speed comes from: fewer parameters, more work done in parallel, or a better loss function. Say why you picked it.
Read only the row names of Table 2 (p. 8), not the numbers. Predict: can a single Transformer beat ensembles of older models on English-German? If yes, by roughly how many BLEU points?

pass2.text: Using Figure 1, explain the three different places the model uses attention. For each one, say where the queries come from and where the keys and values come from.
Explain why the decoder's self-attention has to be masked while the encoder's self-attention does not.
Suppose you deleted the positional encodings and changed nothing else. Predict what the model could no longer tell apart, and give two short sentences it would confuse.

pass3.text: Assume each component of q and k is independent with mean 0 and variance 1, and d_k = 64. What is the variance of q·k? What do you divide by to bring it back to 1?
The base model uses 8 heads with d_k = d_v = 64 instead of 1 head with d_k = d_v = 512. Explain why the total compute stays about the same.
Using the per-layer complexities in Table 1, compare self-attention and a recurrent layer for a sentence of n = 50 tokens with d = 512. Which is cheaper per layer, and by roughly what factor?

pass4.text: Table 3 rows (B) show that a smaller key size d_k hurts quality, and the authors suggest a better compatibility function might help. Look at the other columns of those rows. What other explanation fits, and what experiment would tell the two apart?

The authors kept sinusoidal positional encodings partly because they may let the model handle longer sentences than it saw in training. Does anything in the paper test this? What would a fair test look like?

Self-attention cost grows with the square of sequence length. Name the kind of input where this makes the Transformer a poor fit, and state the fix the paper itself proposes, including what that fix costs.

debrief.text: What were the authors trying to accomplish?
What are the key elements of the approach?
Which references do you want to follow, and why?
